frozen_claim: Tracer influx into perivascular spaces is a valid quantitative proxy for net parenchymal solute clearance.

observable.name: spearman_rho_influx_vs_net_parenchymal_clearance
observable.definition: Spearman rank correlation between imaged perivascular influx (influx = Q*C0, the through-flow delivered into the PVS conduit) and net parenchymal clearance (clearance = g*C_p, with series exchange-egress conductance g = E*K/(E+K) and parenchymal concentration C_p = Q*C0/(Q+g)) across a Monte-Carlo box of N=30000 points per regime. PVS through-flow Q, PVS<->ISF exchange E and ISF->vasculature egress K are independent log-uniform draws; the in-channel Peclet number is held in [0.1, 10] for every point so the neutral imaging substrate is preserved and never pins E or K. The proxy is judged valid only if influx ranks clearance tightly across the plausible box and no named single-mechanism bottleneck breaks the rank ordering.

model.generative: Steady-state, well-mixed two-compartment series-conductance transport model. The imaged PVS conduit delivers influx = Q*C0; solute then crosses into interstitium with exchange conductance E and leaves to the vasculature with egress conductance K, combining as the series conductance g = E*K/(E+K); the steady parenchymal concentration is C_p = Q*C0/(Q+g) and net clearance is g*C_p. Q, E and K are physically independent, so the imaged delivery step and the rate-limiting exchange/egress step can decouple.
model.config: C0=1.0, N=30000 samples per regime, seed=11. Plausible box: Q, E, K all log-uniform 10^[-1,1]. Conduit-limited regime: E,K log-uniform 10^[1.5,2.5] so g>>Q. Vascular-egress bottleneck: K log-uniform 10^[-2.5,-1.5], Q,E normal. Interstitial-exchange bottleneck: E log-uniform 10^[-2.5,-1.5], Q,K normal. Egress depth scan: shift the K band down by s decades for s in {0,-0.5,-1.0,-1.5,-2.0}. Peclet held log-uniform in [0.1,10] across all regimes.
model.controls: The neutral Peclet substrate is preserved identically across every regime, so a drop in the influx-clearance correlation cannot be attributed to changing the imaging channel; it can only come from the independent exchange/egress conductance becoming rate-limiting. The conduit-limited regime is the positive control where the proxy is expected to hold (g>>Q).

thresholds.decision_rule: PRO is accepted only if the Spearman influx-clearance correlation is >= 0.8 across the full plausible box AND no named physiologically plausible bottleneck breaks the rank ordering. PRO is rejected if a physiologically plausible bottleneck yields rho <= 0.3 or reverses ranks while preserving the neutral Peclet substrate.

failure_modes: Synthetic substrate only: the true in vivo ranges and covariances of Q, E and K are unknown, so this cannot establish that real glymphatic transport lives in a bottleneck regime - the decisive external-validity limitation.

Independence is assumed: if Q and E (or K) covary in vivo - e.g. all rising together with pressure or arterial pulsatility - the influx-clearance coupling could be restored, which this independent-draw box does not test.
Steady-state only: transient accumulation, lag, and wash-in/wash-out dynamics are not modelled and could shift the correlation in either direction.
The perivenous PVS-efflux pathway that breaks the conservation-of-mass argument is represented structurally (as an egress route) but is not calibrated to any tracer or imaging data.
accepted_evidence_criteria: The thesis is supported on this substrate only if influx ranks net clearance with Spearman rho >= 0.8 across the full plausible box and no named single-mechanism bottleneck (vascular egress, interstitial exchange, or a depressed-egress depth band) drops rho to or below 0.3 or reverses ranks.
rejected_evidence_criteria: The thesis is rejected on this substrate if a physiologically plausible bottleneck yields rho <= 0.3 or reverses ranks while the neutral Peclet substrate is preserved. This synthetic sufficiency test cannot establish the REAL-DATA version of the claim even when the thesis fails here; that would require in vivo measurement of influx and net clearance under a documented egress bottleneck with the true Q,E,K covariance structure.
